keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no area; a 25 km circle round Lagos (about 2,000 km2) stands for the island, lagoon shore and mainland strip of the colony proper. The protectorate over Yorubaland (1890-1897) is in the vassal events, not in this shape.

ledger.note: 1861 (6 August): Britain annexes Lagos. 'Lagos was annexed on 6 August 1861 under the threat of force by Commander Beddingfield'; Oba Dosunmu resisted 'for 11 days' before signing the Lagos Treaty of Cession; the colony was declared on 5 March 1862 (infobox 'Established: 5 March 1862').
1891 (13 August): Ilaro comes under British protection. 'On 13 August 1891, a treaty placed the kingdom of Ilaro under British protection.'
1892: Lagos attacks Ijebu. 'Carter attacked Ijebu in 1892' (Lagos Colony page); the Ijebu Ode page has the landing at Epe on 12 May 1892 and the capture of Ijebu Ode.
1892: Ijebu Ode is captured and the Awujale surrenders 'shortly afterward' (no month on the page).

1892: the Ijebu kingdom passes under the Lagos Colony's protectorate. The page puts a protectorate 'over most of Yorubaland between 1890 and 1897' and says Carter attacked Ijebu in 1892; the Ijebu pages say the kingdom was later annexed to Southern Nigeria (undated).
1893 (3 February): the Alafin of Oyo accepts British protection. 'On 3 February 1893, Carter signed a treaty of protection with the Alafin of Oyo.'

1893 (15 August): Ibadan accepts a protectorate. 'On 15 August 1893, a protectorate agreement was signed with Ibadan' (Lagos Colony page); the Ibadan page: Fijabi, Baale of Ibadan, with the acting Governor George C. Denton.
1906 (28 February): the Yoruba protectorate is merged with Southern Nigeria. 'The protectorate was incorporated into the Southern Nigeria Protectorate in February 1906.'
1906 (28 February): Ijebu becomes part of the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria.
1906 (28 February): Oyo becomes part of the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria.
1906 (28 February): Ibadan becomes part of the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria.

1906 (28 February): Lagos is amalgamated with Southern Nigeria. 'On 28 February 1906, the two territories were amalgamated as the combined territory called the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria.'

certainty.note: No area and no boundary on the page; the colony proper is a circle round Lagos, the protectorate states are circles round their capitals. The 1861 cession and the 1906 amalgamation are firmly dated.

notes: Lagos Colony has no Cliopatria row (Cliopatria's British Africa, af-08, starts 1885 and draws British Africa as an aggregate). Three pages opened (two shared with other dossiers). The page gives no area; the colony proper is a 25 km circle at Lagos. Administrative history not drawn: Lagos merged with Sierra Leone in 1866, was transferred to the Gold Coast in 1874 and became a separate colony again in 1886 (page). The Egba (Abeokuta) and Ijebu 1888 treaties named in some sources are not on this page, which gives 1890s treaty dates only for Ilaro, Oyo and Ibadan; the Egba United Government, the Ilorin Emirate and New Oyo have no dossiers. Disagreement: Egerton's departure 16 February 1906 (governors table) vs 28 February 1906 (text and infobox). Counterparts without dossier: kingdom-of-lagos, new-oyo, Ilaro (Yewa kingdom).
